title: Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) Claim Timing Reference Card
content:
**Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) — claim timing figures for surviving spouses**

These figures govern the dates on which a DIC claim and related claims take effect. They are the same in every rate category: DIC Surviving Spouse (Basic Rate), DIC Surviving Spouse (Basic Rate with 8-Year Provision), DIC Surviving Spouse (Housebound), DIC Surviving Spouse (Housebound with 8-Year Provision), DIC Surviving Spouse (Aid and Attendance) and DIC Surviving Spouse (Aid and Attendance with 8-Year Provision).

| Item | Figure | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| DIC claim window | 365 calendar days | Days after the veteran's death within which a DIC claim takes the first day of the month of death as its effective date |
| Start of payment on a timely claim | The first day of the month of death | The first entitlement month paid when the claim is timely is the month in which the veteran died, from its first day |
| Intent-to-file validity period | 365 calendar days | Days after VA receives an intent to file during which a DIC claim takes the date of that intent to file |
| Accrued-benefits claim window | 365 calendar days | Days after the veteran's death within which a claim for benefits due and unpaid to the veteran must be filed |
| Veteran's payment for the month of death | Released to the surviving spouse | The veteran's payment for the month of death is released to the surviving spouse |

### Points of reading

- All three windows are counted in calendar days, not business days.
- The DIC claim window and the accrued-benefits claim window both run from the date of the veteran's death; the intent-to-file validity period runs from the date VA receives the intent to file.
- When a claim is timely, entitlement is paid from the month of death itself, starting on its first day, whatever day of that month the death occurred.

### Hypothetical dates

- The veteran dies on a day in the middle of a month. A timely DIC claim takes the first day of that same month as its effective date, so that month is the first entitlement month paid.
- An intent to file is received on a given day. A DIC claim received 365 calendar days or fewer after that day falls within the intent-to-file validity period; a claim received on the 366th day after it does not.
